Add one analysis for each scenario and simulation to a plan

Source: R/plan.R
add_analyses.Rd

add_analyses() adds the analysis kind name to the plnr plan p: one analysis for each scenario and simulation of scenarios, and for each combination of the extra dimensions in ....

Usage

add_analyses(p, scenarios, name, fn, ..., control = FALSE)

Arguments

p

A plan from plnr::Plan$new().

scenarios

The scenarios of the run, from scenarios().

name

The name of the analysis kind, for example "models". It is the name of the element of the results object. It MUST be a syntactic name that starts with a letter. It MUST NOT be "manifest" or "exclusions", and it MUST NOT start with "pbn_". Each kind of one plan MUST have its own name. save_results() names the exclusion table of a cohort exclusions.

fn

The action function, function(data, argset).

...

The extra dimensions, each named, for example outcome = CFG$outcomes. Each MUST be an atomic vector with at least one value, with no NA and no value twice. A vector of length 1 is a constant of the kind.

control

TRUE adds the kind to every fake scenario of scenarios, and never to "real". Use it for a check that is not a result, for example a model without adjustment that a fake scenario tests.

Value

Invisibly, the names of the analyses of the kind, in the order of the plan.

Details

Each analysis gets the name <scenario>__sim_<kkkk>__<name>__<i>, for example null__sim_0003__models__2. <kkkk> is the simulation with four digits, also for a scenario with 1 simulation. <i> counts the combinations of the extra dimensions from 1, with the last dimension of ... changing fastest. A kind without extra dimensions has <i> 1. To step through one analysis by hand, use get_argset() and get_data(). They take the scenario, the simulation, the kind and <i>, so you do not type the name.

The argset of each analysis holds these fields:

  • scenario, sim, and analysis, the kind name.

  • seed, the seed of the analysis.

  • the value of each extra dimension.

  • the value of each setting column of its scenario.

The name of an extra dimension MUST follow these rules:

  • It MUST be syntactic.

  • It MUST NOT be the name of a setting column.

  • It MUST NOT be one of scenario, sim, analysis, seed, index_analysis, name, fn, fn_name, data and argset.

pbn adds fn in a wrapper. The wrapper calls set.seed(argset$seed) and then fn(data, argset). fn runs inside the wrapper, so plnr::is_run_directly() is FALSE in it when the plan runs.

The seed depends on the kind name, the counter <i> and sim only:

  • It does not depend on the order of the analyses, the worker count or the R session.

  • Two kinds of one simulation get different seeds, so they draw different numbers.

  • One kind gets the same seed in each scenario, so its draws in null and in real of one simulation are the same.

  • It is 10000 or more, so it differs from the seed sim of the data of simulations 1 to 9999.

The seed is a polynomial hash with base 257, modulo the prime 2147483629, of the code points of "<name>__<i>__<sim>", plus 10000. Two analyses of one simulation with the same seed stop add_analyses() with an error that names both kinds.

While run_plan() runs, an analysis fails when it changes the shared data in place. plnr gives every analysis of one scenario and simulation the same object. pbn compares the names, the number of rows, the data.table key and the address of each column of each data.frame before and after the analysis. That finds an added, removed, renamed or replaced column, for example data$d[, x := 1], and a new key from data.table::setkey(). It does not find a change of values in place: data$d[1, x := 0], data$d[g == "a", y := 0], data.table::set() on some rows, data.table::setorder() and data.table::setattr() on a column. Copy the data first with data.table::copy() when the analysis changes it.

For each scenario and simulation, pbn also adds one analysis named <scenario>__sim_<kkkk>__pbn_n_rows. It counts the rows of each data element. save_results() stores the counts in manifest$n_rows_data, and leaves the analysis out of the results.

add_analyses() stops before it adds anything when an analysis of that name is in the plan already.

See also

vignette("pbn"), which builds and runs a small fake project.

Other plan: add_data(), cohort_data(), get_data(), run_plan()

Examples

CFG <- list(
  scenarios = data.frame(scenario = c("real", "null"), sims = c(1, 2)),
  outcomes = c("y1", "y2")
)
p <- plnr::Plan$new()
pbn::add_data(p, "d", fn = function(scenario, sim) {
  return(data.frame(y1 = stats::rnorm(5), y2 = stats::rnorm(5)))
})
pbn::add_analyses(
  p,
  pbn::scenarios(CFG),
  name = "means",
  fn = function(data, argset) {
    return(data.frame(mean = mean(data$d[[argset$outcome]])))
  },
  outcome = CFG$outcomes
)
pbn::get_argset(p, "null", 2, "means", 2)
#> $scenario
#> [1] "null"
#> 
#> $sim
#> [1] 2
#> 
#> $analysis
#> [1] "means"
#> 
#> $seed
#> [1] 1380106697
#> 
#> $outcome
#> [1] "y2"
#>
